_comment: Jargon term -> one everyday sentence. Read by lib/ac_gloss.py: when the promise text of a question to the operator contains a term, the question appends the gloss (at most 2, in order of first appearance). Keys are lower case; matching is whole-word and case-insensitive.

terms.commit: a saved snapshot of the work, kept in the project history
terms.pull request: a proposal to add finished work to the main version, which others can review first
terms.stack profile: the ready-made set of technology choices a project starts from
terms.gate: an automatic check that must pass before work moves on
terms.phase: one stage of the overall process, such as planning, building or testing
terms.pipeline: the fixed sequence of stages a project goes through
terms.review model: the AI that reads the work and gives an opinion
terms.reviewer model: the AI that reads the work and gives an opinion
terms.build: the stage where the software is actually written
terms.deployment: putting the finished software where people can use it
terms.coordinator: the part that hands out tasks and keeps track of them
terms.campaign: a planned series of related changes worked through one after another
terms.branch: a separate line of work that does not disturb the main version
terms.merge: joining finished work into the main version
terms.repository: the place where all of a project's files and history are kept
terms.hook: a small automatic action that runs when something specific happens
terms.schema: the agreed shape that a file or piece of data must have
terms.scaffold: a ready-made starting structure for a new project
terms.dashboard: a page that shows the current status at a glance
terms.changelog: the list of what changed in each release
terms.lint: an automatic check for common mistakes in the code
terms.worktree: a second working copy of the project, so two jobs do not get in each other's way
terms.iterate: one round of changing an existing project
terms.catalog: the list of promises the product makes
terms.traceability: being able to follow a requirement through to the work and tests that cover it
